proposals.before: Before he was twenty-some years old he was already enfeoffed as a general, sharing rank with his father.
proposals.after: Before he was twenty-some years old he was already appointed as a general, sharing rank with his father.
proposals.reason: 拜將軍 is appointment to general's rank, not an enfeoffment.

proposals.before: The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to read the heavens; Xianzhi was afraid to advance, and Bian Lingcheng was afraid as well.
proposals.after: The emperor had sent the diviner Han Lübing to observe the sun; Lübing feared and did not wish to go on, and Bian Lingcheng also feared.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names no subject 仙芝 before 懼不欲行; the nearest agent is 術士韓履冰, and 邊令誠亦懼 treats that fear as shared with the envoy. The idiomatic English invents Xianzhi as the fearful subject.

proposals.before: He ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge at once. Greater Bolü lay sixty li beyond; the bridge was severed only at dusk, and Tibetan forces were already pouring in — too late to stop them.
proposals.after: He ordered Yuanqing to cut the vine bridge at once. Bolü still lay sixty li away; the bridge was severed only at dusk, and Tibetan forces were already pouring in — too late to stop them.
proposals.reason: 去勃律猶六十里 names 勃律, not 大勃律; the idiomatic rendering invents Greater Bolü.

proposals.before: In the ninth month they returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and rejoined Bian Lingcheng's detachment.
proposals.after: In the ninth month they returned to Lianyunbao on the Bole River and met Bian Lingcheng and the others.
proposals.reason: Chinese 與邊令誠等相見 is a meeting with Bian Lingcheng and others, not a reunion with a detachment.

proposals.before: When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one from the capital to welcome or comfort them; he cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
proposals.after: When Xianzhi's army returned to Hexi, Fumeng Lingcha sent no one to welcome or comfort them; he cursed Xianzhi, saying: "Dog-gut-eating Korean slave!
proposals.reason: 都不使人迎勞 does not mention the capital; 京 is an insertion.

proposals.before: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from Shi he obtained more than ten large stones of kingfisher feathers, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in abundance.
proposals.after: Xianzhi was greedy by nature; from Shi he obtained more than ten large lumps of se-se gemstone, five or six camels' loads of pure gold, and famous horses and precious jades in abundance.
proposals.reason: 瑟瑟 here are gemstone blocks counted in 石, not kingfisher feathers.

proposals.before: if you judge by looks alone, you may lose another Zilu!"
proposals.after: if you judge by looks alone, you may lose another Ziyu!"
proposals.reason: Chinese 子羽 is Tantai Mieming's courtesy name (the Analects warning against judging by looks), not Zilu (子路).

proposals.before: if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose them as with Zilu!"
proposals.after: if you take men by appearance, I fear you will lose them as with Ziyu!"
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 子羽 is Ziyu, not Zilu.

proposals.before: When his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty years of age, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was Commander-in-Chief — quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he had more than thirty personal attendants in memorial, their clothes bright and fresh.
proposals.after: When his grandfather died, Changqing was orphaned and poor; past thirty years of age, it happened that Fumeng Lingcha was Military Commissioner of the Four Garrisons and General Gao Xianzhi was Commander-in-Chief — quite talented; whenever he went on campaign he memorialized more than thirty personal attendants, their clothes bright and fresh.
proposals.reason: 奏傔從 means requesting/registering attendants by memorial, not attendants who exist "in memorial".

proposals.before: Changqing sent his best horsemen against the Tujue vanguard and killed several hundred rebels.
proposals.after: Changqing sent his best horsemen against the Zhejie vanguard and killed several hundred rebels.
proposals.reason: 柘羯 names Central Asian Zhejie auxiliaries, not the Tujue as a people; the idiomatic rendering substitutes the wrong ethnonym.

proposals.before: He withdrew to Xuaren Gate and was defeated again.
proposals.after: He withdrew to Xuanren Gate and was defeated again.
proposals.reason: 宣仁門 is Xuanren Gate; Xuaren drops the n of 仁.

proposals.before: At Tong Pass Lingcheng led Changqing to the lane south of the post station and read the edict of execution.
proposals.after: At Tong Pass, Lingcheng led Changqing to the lane south of the post station and read the edict of execution.
proposals.reason: Missing comma fuses the place Tong Pass with the person Lingcheng, which also produced a spurious fused candidate.

proposals.before: I read in the Spring and Autumn that Langchen said he had not yet found his place to die — I have found mine.
proposals.after: I read in the Spring and Autumn that Lang Shen said he had not yet found his place to die — I have found mine.
proposals.reason: 狼瞫 is the Jin officer Lang Shen; Langchen fuses surname and given name.

proposals.before: Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said, "Feng, you rose from nothing; I made you my judge, then you replaced me as commissioner, and today we die together — is this fate?"
proposals.after: Xianzhi looked at Changqing's corpse and said, "Feng the Second, you rose from nothing; I made you my judge, then you replaced me as commissioner, and today we die together — is this fate?"
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 二 from 封二, which is a ranked childhood/courtesy designation ('Feng the Second'), not the bare surname Feng.

proposals.before: He first served Commissioner Wang Yi; when Yi attacked Xincheng he put Han in charge of strategy, and the whole army stood in awe of him.
proposals.after: He first served Commissioner Wang Chui; when Chui attacked Xincheng he put Han in charge of strategy, and the whole army stood in awe of him.
proposals.reason: 王倕 is Wang Chui (倕), not Wang Yi; the English given name does not match the Chinese character.

proposals.before: Han was summoned to court; the emperor was pleased with him and made him Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, prefect of Xiping, acting censor-in-chief, and Longyou commissioner in Zhongsi's place.
proposals.after: Han was summoned to court; the emperor was pleased with him and made him Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials (Honglu qing), prefect of Xiping, acting Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, and acting Longyou commissioner for disbursements and military colonies in Zhongsi's place, in charge of commission affairs.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚卿 is the Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness (a rendering of 開府/光祿-type titles). The idiomatic line also collapses 支度營田副大使，知節度事.

proposals.before: The emperor rewarded him with special advancement, acting Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, a fifth-rank post for a son, a thousand bolts of silk, a manor, and acting censor-in-chief.
proposals.after: The emperor rewarded him with Special Advancement, acting supernumerary Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, a fifth-rank post for a son, a thousand bolts of goods, a manor and a residence, and acting Censor-in-Chief.
proposals.reason: 鴻臚員外卿 is again the Court of State Ceremonial, not Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; 莊宅各一所 is a manor and a residence, and 物 is goods not specifically silk.

proposals.before: When An Lushan rebelled, after Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi's defeats the emperor recalled Han and made him vanguard commander of the heir's army, with Tian Liangqiu as campaigning major and Wang Sili, Huoba Guiren, and others as deputies — two hundred thousand Hexi, Shuofang, and tribal troops with Xianzhi's veterans to hold Tong Pass.
proposals.after: When An Lushan rebelled, because Feng Changqing and Gao Xianzhi had been defeated, the emperor summoned Han and appointed him Vanguard Commander of the Heir Apparent's Army; Tian Liangqiu was made Vice Censor-in-Chief and Campaigning Major; Wang Sili, Qian'er Dafu, Li Chengguang, Su Fading, Guan Chongsi, and the barbarian generals Huoba Guiren, Li Wuding, Hun E, Qibi Ning, and others were made deputy generals — Hexi, Longyou, and Shuofang troops and barbarian soldiers together with Gao Xianzhi's old troops, two hundred thousand in all, to resist the rebels at Tong Pass.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits named deputies present in the Chinese and renders 御史中丞 as if it were only campaigning major, collapsing 河隴 as well.

proposals.before: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan held Hebei he lacked popular support — hold the pass, wear him down, let his followers split, and destroy him without heavy losses.
proposals.after: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan had seized the Hebei-Shuofang region he lacked popular support — hold firm and wear them down, let them split of themselves, and destroy this bandit without heavy losses.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic 'Hebei' undertranslates 河朔, which the literal correctly treats as Hebei and Shuofang.

proposals.before: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian Henan, Lu Yong Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
proposals.after: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian Henan, Lu Jiong Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
proposals.reason: 魯炅 is Lu Jiong, not Lu Yong; the fused 'Lai Tian Henan' / 'Lu Yong Nanyang' also obscures the place names.

proposals.before: Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Yong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."
proposals.after: Your Majesty is the lord who sets chaos aright; the realm is not yet pacified — Li Guangbi is at Tumen, Lai Tian in Henan, Lu Jiong at Nanyang; only keep your servant — with a short letter your servant will summon them, and in no many days it will be pacified."
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise romanizes 炅 as Yong instead of Jiong.

decisions.reason: 拜將軍 is appointment to general's rank; 封 would be enfeoffment. The original 'enfeoffed' misreads 拜.
懼不欲行 has no 仙芝; the nearest agent is 韓履冰, and 邊令誠亦懼 pairs that fear with the envoy. The original invents Xianzhi as the fearful subject.

decisions.reason: 去勃律猶六十里 names 勃律, not 大勃律; 'Greater Bolü' is not in the Chinese.
與邊令誠等相見 is a meeting with Bian Lingcheng and others; 'detachment' is not in the Chinese.
都不使人迎勞 says he sent no one to welcome them; it does not mention the capital.
大塊瑟瑟十餘石 are large lumps of se-se gemstone counted in 石, not kingfisher feathers.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 若以貌取人，恐失之子羽矣

decisions.reason: The literal likewise misreads 子羽 as Zilu; the source names Ziyu.
奏傔從三十餘人 is listing or requesting attendants by memorial, not attendants who exist 'in memorial'.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 每出軍，奏傔從三十餘人

decisions.reason: 宣仁門 is Xuanren Gate; Xuaren drops the n of 仁.

decisions.reason: 狼瞫 is the Jin officer Lang Shen; Langchen fuses the surname 狼 and given name 瞫.
封二 is the ranked address 'Feng the Second'; dropping 二 leaves only the surname.
王倕 is Wang Chui; Yi does not match 倕.

decisions.reason: 鴻臚卿 is Chamberlain for Court Ceremonials, not 開府/光祿 'Grand Master of Splendid Happiness'; 攝御史中丞 is Palace Aide to the Censor-in-Chief, and 支度營田副大使，知節度事 must not be collapsed.

decisions.after: Han had repeatedly urged that though Lushan had seized Hebei he lacked popular support — hold firm and wear them down, let them split of themselves, and destroy this bandit without heavy losses.
decisions.reason: 河朔 here is Hebei north of the Yellow River, not Shuofang; but 持重以弊之 is hold firm, not hold the pass, and 擒茲寇 is this bandit. The proposal's Hebei-Shuofang gloss is too specific.

decisions.after: Your Majesty is heaven's chosen restorer; the realm is not yet settled — Li Guangbi holds Tumen, Lai Tian is in Henan, Lu Jiong in Nanyang; keep me and I will summon them by letter, and peace will come in days."
decisions.reason: 魯炅 is Lu Jiong, not Lu Yong, but the proposed line still fuses person and place as 'Lai Tian Henan' / 'Lu Jiong Nanyang'; 來填在河南，魯炅在南陽 needs the locatives.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 李光弼在土門，來填在河南，魯炅在南陽

decisions.reason: The literal already places each man with 在; only the romanization of 炅 as Yong is wrong and should be Jiong.
